replan_request.reason: RequestBodyLimitMiddleware (starlette/middleware/body_limit.py) rejects on Content-Length as soon as the outermost limited app sees the request, in `__call__` where `too_large` is computed and `_reject` is called, before routing. With Starlette(max_body_size=10) and Route(max_body_size=100), a 50-byte POST that carries a Content-Length header is therefore answered with 413 at the app level. The inner route never gets to raise the limit, which ACC10 requires. ACC9 also requires the Content-Length fail-fast to hold when the endpoint never reads the body. The two requirements can be met together if the outermost middleware defers its fail-fast until the effective limit is final. Concretely: when the declared length exceeds the outer limit, run the app and let inner limited apps apply their own Content-Length check. If the app returns without having started a response and the final scope limit is still lower than the declared length, send the 413 instead. The `received > limit` check in `limited_receive` already reads the limit dynamically. T2 already contains the wiring in routing.py and applications.py, and only tests/test_max_body_size.py remains to be written once body_limit.py is fixed.
